seal.header: flags(1) [part(1) = (i-1)<<4 | (n-1), mid(6)] ; flags: Z=0x01 J=0x02 M=0x04 S=0x08, 0xF0 reserved; part+mid present iff M (n>1)
seal.plaintext: [len(1) UTF-8 sender, iff S, part 1 only] || body (codebook v2 iff Z, else UTF-8)
seal.rejoin: concat over i of text_i + (' ' if J_i else '')

fields.positive[].parts[].payload_hex: exact bytes that went into AES-GCM (sender field + body)

fields.negative[]: every line must FAIL to open with the given keyring
fields.messages[]: open all lines, then assemble: exactly these complete messages may result

positive.note: Compact parts cut at a space that is consumed: J=1 on every part but the last. Rejoin is exact (S1 needed a heuristic here).
No spaces at all: compact parts are cut mid-word (J=0) and still rejoin exactly. S1's stitcher would insert a space at each cut.
Sealer policy: the codebook may lowercase dictionary words, so parts[].plaintext can differ from the input in letter case only.
Sender sealed inside the ciphertext (flags bit S): [len][UTF-8 name] then body. Any holder of the circle key can claim any name.
Sender field only in part 1; S=0 on later parts.
Sender field precedes the codebook body.
Circle name is case-preserving in salt and AAD.
Two circles share slug 'sigi'; the GCM tag decides.
Token buried in other text.
A loose ' #name' after the token is not part of S2; the sender is the sealed 'Steve'.

negative.reason: Last tag byte flipped.
First ciphertext byte flipped.
First nonce byte flipped.
First byte of the sealed sender name flipped (inside the ciphertext).
S bit cleared: the header is in the AAD.
S bit set on a token without a sender field.
Z bit cleared on a codebook part. No lenient fallback in S2.
Z bit set on a raw part. (S1 accepted '.z' added; S2 does not.)
J bit cleared on part 1 of a compact message: rejoin info is authenticated.
J set on the last part: rejected before decryption.
Reserved header bit set: rejected (future format).
Part 1/3 relabelled 2/3: the part byte is in the AAD.
Part 1/3 relabelled 1/2.
Part 1/3 rewritten as a single-part frame (M cleared, part+mid removed).
Part 2 of message B given message A's id to splice it into A: the id is in the AAD.
Same name, different passphrase.
Sealed under 'sigil-vector-other' (same slug, same passphrase); name is in salt and AAD.
An S1 blob presented as S2: different AAD domain (S1 AAD starts 'SIGIL.v1', S2 with the header).
Slug matches no circle.
Frame shorter than header + nonce + tag.
No token.
